blocking_concerns.title: Plan must include explicit per-phase carve-out of _run_pipeline
blocking_concerns.rationale: Non-negotiable #7 forbids both mechanical extraction and punting. _run_pipeline at orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:20799 is now ~2,937 lines (vs ~2,300 cited in the issue). _run_implement_phase_slices exists at line 15913 already, but _run_refine_phase, _run_plan_phase, _run_pr_phase do NOT exist as module-level defs (verified via `grep '^def _run_(refine|plan|pr)_phase'`). The plan must call out the per-phase extraction strategy explicitly (which phase first, how the orchestration loop stays thin, how the BRC consensus + signal handling sequencing is preserved). If the plan ducks this — proposing 'pipelines.py decomposed as a follow-up' or 'mechanical extraction with a permanent allowlist exception' — NACK.
blocking_concerns.nack_trigger: Plan that lacks a concrete per-phase extraction sequence for _run_pipeline, OR plan that defers _run_pipeline carve-out to a separate issue, OR plan that proposes leaving _run_pipeline allowlisted.

blocking_concerns.title: Plan must address the allowlist serialization bottleneck
blocking_concerns.rationale: scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml is a strict-ordered YAML mapping (lines 22-70). 15 of 17 entries are 2 adjacent lines each; 2 (plan_parser.py, phases.py) are 9-line entries with comment blocks. Git cannot dict-merge YAML, so two concurrent slices removing neighboring entries will conflict on the same hunk. The pipeline was given concurrency cap 4 (slice_admit.cap=4 from BRC state). Without a serialization strategy — explicit serialize-on-allowlist, rebase-before-propose discipline, or single-writer ordering — slices will collide and create wasted re-review cycles. This is the recurring failure mode that contributed to the #2261-v3..v10 cancellations (six prior pipelines failed without landing a single slice).
blocking_concerns.nack_trigger: Plan that does not name the allowlist-yaml as a serialization point, OR plan that schedules >1 parallel slice modifying the allowlist without a merge-conflict protocol, OR plan that ignores the 9-line comment blocks for plan_parser.py / phases.py (the comment-block lines are also load-bearing for cq-5 retagging).

blocking_concerns.nack_trigger: Plan whose task list does not include plan_parser.py as a decomposition target, OR plan that lists plan_parser.py as 'out of scope / tracked under #2569'.

blocking_concerns.title: Plan must address barrel re-export audit for in-function lazy imports
blocking_concerns.rationale: orchestrator/routes/phases.py has 8 in-function lazy imports of routes.pipelines symbols (lines 405, 535, 612, 711, 733, 1010, 1189, 1307) and orchestrator/mcp_tools.py has 2 (lines 1609 _read_phase_draft, 1680 _pipeline_identifier). All use the single-prefix `from routes.pipelines import …` shape. These are EASY to miss in an external-importer audit because they are NOT at module top — a `git grep '^from routes.pipelines'` will not surface them. Pattern doc §(d)'s audit recipe must be applied per slice to lazy imports too. If the plan does not call out lazy-import audits explicitly, slices that drop a symbol from the barrel will break phases.py / mcp_tools.py at runtime with opaque ImportError inside a function body — typically surfaced only when that code path is hit in production.
blocking_concerns.nack_trigger: Plan whose pipelines.py slice does not list 'audit in-function lazy imports of routes.pipelines symbols across all importers, not just module-top imports' as an explicit step.

blocking_concerns.title: Plan must respect non-negotiable #8 for gateway.py: 47 Flask @app.route decorators stay in __init__.py
blocking_concerns.rationale: gateway/gateway.py has 47 @app.route( decorators (e.g. line 936 GET /api/v1/health, line 1084 POST /api/v1/config/reload, line 1112 POST /api/v1/git/push). #2261 HITL decision-8 (carried forward as non-negotiable #8) requires decorators to stay in __init__.py with thin wrappers delegating to submodule bodies. This is mechanical but error-prone — 47 wrappers must be authored. If the plan proposes moving decorators into submodules (or uses Flask blueprints to side-step the convention without operator sign-off), it breaks the operator-locked HITL decision-8.
blocking_concerns.nack_trigger: Plan whose gateway.py slice proposes moving @app.route decorators into submodules, OR plan that introduces Flask blueprints for gateway routes without first registering a new HITL decision to supersede #2261 decision-8.

top_3_risks: RISK-1 (program-discipline): six prior pipelines on the same surface (#2261-v3..v10) cancelled without merging a single slice. Without conservative slicing and bounded concurrency, #2817 inherits the same failure mode.

RISK-2 (technical): _run_pipeline per-phase refactor is the structural high-water mark. ~2,937 lines, holds the BRC consensus state machine + signal handling + slice DAG + HITL gates. Extraction must preserve sequencing exactly; #2319 unit-test follow-up is the safety net.

RISK-3 (operational): scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml is the serialization bottleneck for the entire program. 17 adjacent entries; git cannot dict-merge YAML; concurrency cap is 4. Conflict choreography must be explicit in the plan.

risks.title: Six prior pipelines on the same surface failed without merging a follow-up slice
risks.evidence: git log --all --grep='2261' shows pipeline state breadcrumbs for #2261-v3, v4, v5, v6, v9, v10 — all 'cancelled' or 'failed' followed by 'Delete pipeline'. No surviving egg/issue-2261* branches. v10 had four commit-authorship entries for coder + documenter roles but no merged slice. Only artifact that survived is #2335 (the pattern + worked reference), merged 2026-04-30.
mitigations: Plan starts with the SMALLEST oversize file (orchestrator/routes/deployment.py at 1,650 lines, only 10% over the cap) as slice-1 to validate the pipeline end-to-end before tackling structural outliers.
Concurrency cap stays at 4 (current slice_admit.cap=4) or lower; the planner should explicitly justify if concurrency goes higher.
Each slice carries its own bisectable step-0 commit (`git mv foo.py foo/__init__.py`) per pattern doc §(b); reviewers can verify the no-op move before reviewing cluster carve-outs.
pipelines.py and gateway.py (the two structural outliers) are NOT slice-1 or slice-2; the planner should sequence them after at least 3-4 smaller decompositions have landed cleanly.
risks.rollback: Each slice is a single PR; reverting one PR rolls back that slice cleanly. The allowlist ratchet means re-adding the entry to scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml is mechanical. No cross-slice rollback coupling unless slices are sub-stacked.

risks.title: _run_pipeline per-phase carve-out is the highest-risk extraction
risks.evidence: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:20799 defines _run_pipeline (~2,937 lines). Only _run_implement_phase_slices exists today at line 15913. _run_refine_phase, _run_plan_phase, _run_pr_phase do not exist as module-level defs — they are inline branches inside _run_pipeline. The function holds the BRC consensus state machine, signal handling (heartbeat / readiness / OVERSEER_ALERT), slice DAG admission, HITL gates, and re-entry semantics.
mitigations: Extract per-phase one at a time (4 sub-slices, not one mega-slice). Each sub-slice extracts ONE phase handler and validates that the orchestration loop is unchanged for the others.

Land #2319 (unit tests for per-phase handlers) ALONGSIDE the pipelines.py decomposition, not as a follow-up. The pattern doc §(c) notes the test follow-up is tracked by #2319 — the planner should explicitly attach #2319 work to the pipelines.py slice family.

Pre-extraction baseline: capture a `pytest tests/orchestrator/routes/test_pipelines.py -q` golden output before slice-1 of pipelines.py lands; reviewer for each subsequent pipelines.py sub-slice compares against it.
The thin orchestration loop must be reviewed for sequencing: signal handling order, BRC re-entry, HITL gate placement — these are the load-bearing invariants.
risks.rollback: Per-phase extraction is per-sub-slice rollback. If a sub-slice surfaces a regression that escapes review, revert just that sub-slice; the orchestration loop falls back to the inline branch for that phase.

risks.title: scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml is a serialization bottleneck under concurrency cap 4
risks.evidence: scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml is 70 lines: caps block (lines 17-21), files: map starts at line 22. 15 entries are 2 adjacent lines each (path + issue:); 2 entries (plan_parser.py lines 53-61; phases.py lines 62-70) carry 7-line comment blocks above 2-line entries. Git cannot dict-merge YAML — two slices removing neighboring entries collide on the same hunk. Concurrency cap is currently 4 (BRC state slice_admit.cap).
mitigations: Plan declares scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml a single-writer surface: at most one slice in flight against the same allowlist hunk window at any time.
Sub-stacking discipline: slices that target adjacent allowlist entries are merged sequentially (rebase-before-propose, not parallel-and-merge).

cq-5 retagging (phases.py from #2261 to #2817; plan_parser.py from #2548 to #2817) lands in whichever slice touches the allowlist first — the planner should NAME that slice explicitly so subsequent slices don't re-do the retag.

The 9-line comment blocks for plan_parser.py and phases.py are removed entirely when those files decompose; the remaining 15 entries shrink to 30 lines, reducing collision surface as the program progresses.
risks.rollback: Allowlist mutations are idempotent re-additions of the dropped entry. Conflict-driven re-review costs cycles but does not corrupt state.

risks.title: In-function lazy imports of routes.pipelines symbols evade module-top import audits
risks.evidence: orchestrator/routes/phases.py has 8 in-function `from routes.pipelines import …` (lines 405, 535, 612, 711, 733, 1010, 1189, 1307). orchestrator/mcp_tools.py has 2: line 1609 (_read_phase_draft), line 1680 (_pipeline_identifier). All single-prefix form. A `git grep '^from routes.pipelines'` (anchored to module top) misses all 10.
mitigations: Each pipelines.py sub-slice runs pattern doc §(d)'s external-importer audit recipe and explicitly looks for in-function imports too (un-anchor the grep pattern: `git grep 'from routes.pipelines'` without `^`).
Barrel __init__.py re-exports every symbol referenced by these 10 lazy imports (list them explicitly in the audit deliverable).

Add a make-test target or pytest fixture that imports every public-and-underscore-prefixed symbol from routes.pipelines as a smoke test; missed re-exports surface as AttributeError at test collection, not at runtime.
risks.rollback: Symbol-restore is mechanical (add the symbol back to __init__.py re-export list); no data corruption.

Re-grep scoped just to tests/ + integration_tests/ returns 7 / 15 / 0 respectively — the broader analysis count includes patch references in sandbox/, shared/, and scripts/. Either way, the barrel must re-export every patched symbol.
mitigations: Pre-extraction audit per slice: `grep -rhE 'patch\("(orchestrator\.)?routes\.pipelines\.[_a-zA-Z0-9]+"' --include='*.py' .` and diff against post-extraction barrel re-exports.
make test-all is the gate (non-negotiable, already in acceptance criteria); a missing patch target surfaces as a collection-time failure.
Pattern doc §(d) already mandates this audit; the plan must reference it explicitly per slice.

risks.title: Reviewer bandwidth and rebase choreography across stacked slices
risks.evidence: Concurrency cap 4 + 17 files = at minimum 5 rounds of 4 parallel slices (one slice per file) plus 1-4 sub-slices for pipelines.py's per-phase extraction. Each rebase forces re-review of the slice. The downstream-reviewer chain (reviewer_code, reviewer_contract, reviewer_test) reviews every re-propose.
mitigations: Plan orders slices to minimize rebases: smallest files first (least review surface) so the reviewer cohort builds confidence early.
Slices are author-rebased on origin/main before proposal, not at merge time.
Reviewer-bandwidth budget: planner should NOT schedule >4 concurrent slices unless the operator has explicitly raised the concurrency cap.
Cohorts can share a documenter slice (e.g. seam-table updates + pattern-doc cq-4 refresh in one slice) to amortize doc-review cost.

rollback_plan_summary: Each slice is a single PR; reverting one PR rolls back that slice cleanly. Allowlist mutations are idempotent (re-add the dropped entry). No cross-slice rollback coupling unless slices are sub-stacked (in which case the planner must call out the sub-stack rollback order in the slice text). For _run_pipeline per-phase carve-out, per-sub-slice rollback restores the inline branch for that phase.
human_review_recommended: Plan's per-phase carve-out strategy for _run_pipeline (RISK-2 / blocker-1): the orchestration loop is the BRC consensus state machine — operator should sanity-check that the sequencing invariants the planner names are complete.
Plan's sub-stacking strategy for pipelines.py (the structural outlier at 24,559 lines): is it 4 sub-slices in one PR family? Or 4 PRs landed sequentially? Operator should confirm reviewer bandwidth.
Plan's packaging decision for stale #2261 → #2817 reference refresh (RISK-7): docs-only-up-front vs inlined-per-slice vs hybrid — operator may want to see the planner's choice and rationale.
